newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Ed says near 200,000 remain without power.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Ed says near 200,000 remain without power.

text.p: Detroit Edison Co said about 200,000 electricity customers in southeast Michigan remained without power as of Thursday morning following severe thunderstorms late Wednesday.
"We had lost service to close to 300,000 customers (Wednesday night) as a result of the storms. We've restored power to about 100,000 of those," said Detroit Edison spokeswoman Lorie Kessler.
Crews continued to make repairs, and power was expected to be restored to 90 to 95 percent of the lost customers by Friday night, the spokeswoman said.
Storm damage knocked down local distribution lines, and Kessler said none of Detroit Edison's major power transmission lines were damaged.
Detroit Edison serves about two million customers in a 7,600-square mile area in southeast Michigan, including the city of Detroit.
